$comment: The pinned upstream sources this package's generated data is built from, following the
pattern of `packages/minecraft/datagen/manifest.json`: every source is a version, a URL
and a hash, so a build is reproducible and an edition bump is an edit to this file plus
a refresh of `pack-hashes.json` beside it.
`utils/fetch/fetch-sources.ts` (the `fetch:sources` script) downloads each source into
`node_modules/.cache/jsprismarine/<source>/<version>/`, verifies the hash before
unpacking, and skips sources whose verified content is already present. For offline
work, `JSP_BDS_PATH`, `JSP_JAVA_JAR_PATH`, `JSP_BEDROCK_SAMPLES_PATH`,
`JSP_VANILLA_MCDOC_PATH` and `JSP_GEYSER_MAPPINGS_PATH` point at local copies and
bypass the download.
Hashes for `bds` and `javaServer` are cross-checked against the research notes in
`docs/research/bedrock-data-extraction.md` and `docs/research/java-datapacks.md`. The
two GitHub archive hashes were measured from codeload on 2026-10-24; GitHub does not
promise byte-stable archives, so if one stops matching, re-verify that the commit is
unchanged and record the new archive hash.
The Linux Bedrock Dedicated Server zip, the only publication with features, feature
rules, structures and worldgen. The CDN resets connections from curl's default
User-Agent, so the fetcher sends a browser one.
Pinned per Bedrock protocol version, so a capture can target a version without
editing this file. Each entry caches under
`node_modules/.cache/jsprismarine/bds/v<protocol>/`, so several versions coexist.
`--protocol <n>` on `fetch:sources` and `dump:bedrock` selects one and
`defaultProtocolVersion` is used when nothing asks; it is the newest release, the
version the server advertises. These are ~95 MB each, so
`fetch:sources` downloads only the selected version rather than every pinned one.
Mojang publishes no checksum beyond a content-md5 header, so each `sha256` was
measured on download. Each `sha1` is Mojang's build hash as recorded by
Bedrock-OSS/BDS-Versions, kept as an independent cross-check of the measured sha256;
both were confirmed to match on 2026-10-29. Mojang makes no retention promise for
older builds: if a download starts failing, the pin has been pulled rather than
corrupted.
`minecraftVersion` is the game version the protocol belongs to; `serverVersion` is
the BDS build number, which carries an extra component and moves independently.
Minecraft Preview 1.26.70.24, from the `bin-linux-preview` channel. The server negotiates
this protocol but advertises the newest release, and cinnabar does not test it; it is
brought up and checked with `pnpm run bringup --protocol 2259`. Replaced, not kept
beside, when the next preview or the 1.26.70 release lands. sha256 measured and sha1
confirmed against Bedrock-OSS/BDS-Versions on 2026-11-15.
Mojang/bedrock-samples, the plain-JSON publication of the vanilla packs plus the
`metadata/vanilladata_modules` files. Read for the 23 items, the item catalog, the
shapes and the trade tables the BDS zip stores as undocumented binary MCB. Pinned
to the commit of the release tag matching the default BDS. The archive hash was
measured from codeload on 2026-11-18, twice, with the same result.
The Java Edition server jar, whose data generator emits the vanilla datapack and the
reports. Pinned per Java Edition release id, the way `bds` is pinned per protocol:
each entry caches as `node_modules/.cache/jsprismarine/java-server/<release>/server.jar`
and its generated data under `<release>/` folders, so several releases coexist.
`--java <release>` on `fetch:sources`, `datagen:java`, `ensure:worldgen` and the other
Java scripts selects one, and `defaultVersion` is used when nothing asks; it is the
release the server runs. `fetch:sources` downloads only the selected jar.
An entry may carry `"preview": true` for a snapshot or pre-release tracked ahead of
the default. At most one entry is a preview, and it must be newer than
`defaultVersion`; loading the manifest fails otherwise.
The default release pairs with `bds.defaultProtocolVersion` and the preview with the
Bedrock preview, or the default protocol without one, for the mapping and item tables.
Any other entry, such as a release pinned before it becomes the default, needs
`"bedrockProtocol": <n>` naming a pinned `bds` protocol; loading the manifest fails
without it.
Each URL and sha1 come from the release's piston-meta package, which is Mojang's own
checksum; the sha1 is also the object name in the URL. Each sha256 was measured on
download. The jar is kept as a file, not unpacked. The data pack format, the data
version and the JDK a release needs are read from the jar's `version.json`, not
written here.
Java Edition 26.4 Snapshot 10, the preview, paired with Bedrock preview 2259. It is
brought up and checked with `pnpm run bringup:java --java 26.4-snapshot-10`. Replaced,
not kept beside, when a snapshot moves the data pack format major, a pre-release ships
or 26.4 is released. sha1 from the version's piston-meta package; sha256 measured on
SpyglassMC/vanilla-mcdoc, the MIT mcdoc schema set `@spyglassmc/mcdoc` checks Java
datapack JSON against. Field-level gating with `#[since=]` and `#[until=]` carries
values up to 26.4, so the pinned 26.3 release is covered. Pinned to the main head
resolved on 2026-10-25.
GeyserMC/mappings, the MIT one-way Java to Bedrock mapping tables. Pinned to the
master head resolved on 2026-10-24.
